claims.text: Standard NiTi exhibits martensitic-transformation-induced plastic deformation behavior.
A minor Cu addition to NiTi can tune the martensitic transformation temperature.
Tuning the martensitic transformation temperature through Cu addition will produce a reversible, temperature-dependent change in deformation behavior.
Cu addition alters phase stability in the NiTi system.
Cu addition modifies the interplay between austenitic and martensitic phases.
Cu addition shifts the martensitic transformation temperature.
Cu addition alters the hysteresis of the martensitic phase transformation.
The Cu-induced compositional variation changes the onset and reversibility of deformation behavior associated with the phase transition.
Changes in transformation temperature and hysteresis make the alloy's plastic deformation behavior strongly temperature-dependent.
Cu-modified NiTi will exhibit a shifted martensitic transformation range relative to unmodified NiTi.
Cu-modified NiTi may exhibit a narrower martensitic transformation range.
The shifted transformation range will produce a pronounced and reversible temperature-dependent change in yield strength or ductility relative to unmodified NiTi.
Standard NiTi without Cu has less tailored temperature-dependent deformation behavior than Cu-modified NiTi.
The desired effect is significant only within an optimal range of Cu content.
Insufficient Cu may fail to produce the desired transformation-temperature shift.
Excessive Cu may fail to produce the desired transformation-temperature shift or may reduce mechanical robustness.
